approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored survivors. It keeps the highest-scoring molecules in score and admission order, chooses breeding parents from high-ranked score bands, and builds fresh structures through connected-fragment crossover and local atom and bond mutations. The first parent supplies the ordinary mutation source or the usually larger crossover core; a separately drawn partner supplies the usually smaller graft. Ordinary multistep mutation and optional crossover finishing remain active, while direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Canonical identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted-score archive uses counts of molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose pool members for evaluation. Accepted offspring update both the model and the live breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove unequal rank probabilities only from the first-parent draw, while preserving exactly the molecules that this draw can already select. The partner keeps its original score-band rule and exclusion of the chosen first molecule. The earlier control made both roles uniform on their original supports, and another also admitted previously unsupported survivors; neither identifies the first role separately. A balanced first-parent scheduler preserved rank preferences but changed dependence between draws, so it addresses a different question. This control keeps independent requests and changes only first-parent rank preference. The prediction is weaker average source quality and possibly lower final scores; the experiment will determine that role's conditional contribution, including any null or beneficial removal result.

hypothesis: Remove nonuniform rank weighting only from each actual first-parent request by sampling uniformly over its exact original positive support after the inherited passive band draw, while retaining the original active score-quantile law and identity exclusion for every crossover-partner request.

finding_summary.headline: First-parent rank preference contributes: its removal lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.072496
finding_summary.insights:
The result localizes useful rank preference to the first-parent role while the crossover partner keeps its original law. Earlier removal from both roles could not establish that distinction. This is positive conditional contribution of first-parent rank weights in the tested composition and three-seed panel; it does not determine the partner’s contribution or permit subtraction of the shared-baseline controls into independent effects. The first parent supplies both ordinary mutation and crossover cores, so their separate values remain open.

More local wins did not mean better search. Strict best-parent beats rose from 629 to 819 and distinct accepted offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,511, but mean best-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.372509 and mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.303045. Sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 237, with mean positive gain falling from 0.022510 to 0.019917. The easier parent reference explains why win counts alone would misread the outcome. Molecular inspection finds abundant rings, aromaticity and recognizable amine/carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive attachments and unresolved geometry and stereochemistry. Larger, decorated families did not consistently reproduce the Parent’s useful compact arrangements, but conventional-bond high-scoring counterexamples remain. Those associations narrow the search-quality problem without establishing a chemical cause of the loss. The fixed first-parent control now has an informative answer; support-only value, chemical mediation, the partner-only control and whole-foundation contribution remain open.

Four task means declined; zaleplon rose by 0.001980. Macro population SD increased from 0.026593 to 0.041376. All task runs completed with their full oracle budgets and no posterior fallback.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive attachments and unspecified stereochemistry; larger structures do not ensure better scores
molecular.overall_character: Algorithm Node n-be83d2b1a4bd produces substituted indole amides and imines, linked nitrogen heterocycles, aryl/cyclic amines, medium-ring carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/dione heterocycles. Rings and aromaticity are abundant: the digest ring-closure incidences range from 0.9460 to 0.9782 and aromatic-text incidences from 0.9425 to 0.9736. These count proposal strings containing a feature, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Every task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. All recorded evaluated optimizer proposal strings parse with the available RDKit; graph parsing does not establish synthesis or stability. Halogen-text incidence ranges from 0.2448 to 0.9897, while explicit charge and stereocentre-text incidence are 0.0 throughout. Clearly protonatable amine candidates are present despite neutral notation. Many saturated and bridged centres have unspecified configuration. The overall chemistry is synthetically questionable and weak in drug-likeness because conventional aromatic, amide and amine regions coexist with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, highly decorated structures and difficult ring junctions. This is not universal: the high-scoring aryl/azetidine family lacks N-halogen, O-halogen and peroxide bonds, and ordinary N-H indole amides also occur. Diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds but leading examples often belong to close local families; different strings are not evidence of independent scaffold coverage. All 15 Child trajectories and all 15 published Parent trajectories were read in full; no supplied path is missing and no task is omitted. Every digest excerpt was reconciled with its Child trajectory. Parent n-62daf219c70a paths match the published-path template in context.evidence_index. The immutable request reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. Comparisons below use those published Parent records, not the changing worktree as Parent authority. Conditions are Research in Depth epoch 1, batch size 10 and 300 observations per task/seed. The Parent baseline reproduced historical n-c55c3d520a2c chemistry under its new profile; the original gap reports in both indexed nodes were read, and their source is retained in the transferable gaps. Historical identity is not an additional independent current comparison. Digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals rather than all seeds' retained best molecules; full trajectories supply the other seeds and best-score pairs. Scores below are observed values rounded to six decimal places unless scientific notation is needed. Heavy-atom and ring counts are RDKit readings of the cited records. Chemistry associations describe output only; they do not establish a missing target pharmacophore, component attribution, activation, biological activity or contribution. The audit and complete path/hash inventory are in .slots/round-0023-slot-2/molecular/trajectory_audit.json.

Seed 2 reaches a 25-heavy-atom partially unsaturated six-membered N-chloro heterocycle linked to an anilide and an O-linked cyanate side chain; its leading structure has two rings, only one aromatic. liabilities: The highest seed-0 molecule has chlorine on the amide nitrogen, chemically distinct from its ordinary carbon-bound aryl fluorine.
The seed-2 family contains N-Cl and O-linked cyanate groups, while other leaders have N-N substitution or imines. Their scores are not stability or synthetic-route evidence.
Tiny late proposals lose almost all functional context; extensive unsaturated substituent changes can also reduce the score while leaving a recognizable scaffold.

Preserve ordinary aryl halogens and useful amine centres when supported by local feedback. This suggests testing environmental plausibility, not a blanket halogen filter; these associations neither establish a score benefit for replacement nor attribute the chemistry to one component.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted, scored survivors. It keeps the highest-scoring molecules in score and admission order, chooses breeding parents from high-ranked score bands, and builds fresh structures through connected-fragment crossover and local atom and bond mutations. The first parent supplies the ordinary mutation source or the usually larger crossover core; a separately drawn partner supplies the usually smaller graft. Ordinary multistep mutation and optional crossover finishing remain active, while direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Canonical identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted-score archive uses counts of molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose pool members for evaluation. Accepted offspring update both the model and the live breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove unequal rank probabilities only from the first-parent draw, while preserving exactly the molecules that this draw can already select. The earlier control made both roles uniform on their original supports, and another also admitted previously unsupported survivors; neither identifies the first role separately. A balanced first-parent scheduler preserved rank preferences but changed dependence between draws, so it addresses a different question. This control keeps independent requests and changes only first-parent rank preference. finding_summary.headline: First-parent rank preference contributes: its removal lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.072496
finding_summary.insights:
The result localizes useful rank preference to the first-parent role while the crossover partner keeps its original law. Earlier removal from both roles could not establish that distinction. This is positive conditional contribution of first-parent rank weights in the tested composition and three-seed panel; it does not determine the partner’s contribution or permit subtraction of the shared-baseline controls into independent effects. The first parent supplies both ordinary mutation and crossover cores, so their separate values remain open.

More local wins did not mean better search. Strict best-parent beats rose from 629 to 819 and distinct accepted offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,511, but mean best-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.372509 and mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.303045. Sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 237, with mean positive gain falling from 0.022510 to 0.019917. The easier parent reference explains why win counts alone would misread the outcome. Molecular inspection finds abundant rings, aromaticity and recognizable amine/carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive attachments and unresolved geometry and stereochemistry. Larger, decorated families did not consistently reproduce the Parent’s useful compact arrangements, but conventional-bond high-scoring counterexamples remain. Those associations narrow the search-quality problem without establishing a chemical cause of the loss. The fixed first-parent control now has an informative answer; support-only value, chemical mediation, the partner-only control and whole-foundation contribution remain open.
finding_summary.results:
Every one of 74,353 first-parent requests preserved the original eligible molecules while changing their probabilities; 71,068 actual identities differed from the inherited choice on the same random state. All 33,811 partner requests retained their original conditional law. Expected first-parent score on the actual populations fell from 0.359600 to 0.334474, and expected topness fell from 0.884224 to 0.755392. Changed first choices reached 3,926 of 4,350 accepted offspring; 2,211 of those offspring later bred. Full accepted-score learning, bounded greedy survival, ordinary graph transformations and all 435 complete candidate-pool selections remained active.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.523174, a paired change of -0.072496 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.156631, -0.029176 and -0.031680. Eleven of fifteen endpoints declined. Four improved: zaleplon seeds 0 and 2 (+0.075655 and +0.010925), median similarity seed 1 (+0.013577), and sitagliptin seed 1 (+0.124636). Four task means declined; zaleplon rose by 0.001980. Macro population SD increased from 0.026593 to 0.041376. All task runs completed with their full oracle budgets and no posterior fallback.

It keeps the highest-scoring molecules in score and admission order, chooses breeding parents from high-ranked score bands, and builds fresh structures through connected-fragment crossover and local atom and bond mutations. Ordinary multistep mutation and optional crossover finishing remain active, while direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Canonical identity checks form a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process fitted to the complete task-local accepted-score archive uses counts of molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose pool members for evaluation. Accepted offspring update both the model and the live breeding population.

A balanced first-parent scheduler preserved rank preferences but changed dependence between draws, so it addresses a different question. This control keeps independent requests and changes only first-parent rank preference.
